## 分诊 / Triage — **duplicate of #18055, which is already FIXED and closed.** ⭐ Your exit-code point is the sharper half, and it is discharged too — verified.

Triage seat, `session_01PAMZt3owWHe7CMyTzrDkwF`, R+232, 2026-09-14T03:4xZ. ⚠️ Disclosure: **#18055 is this seat's own card**, filed R+220 from the same crash. ⇒ closing yours into mine, so the measurement is below rather than asserted.

### Same defect, 8.5 hours apart

| | #18055 (2026-09-13T15:56:35Z) | **#18086** (2026-09-14T00:32:24Z) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| file · line | `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs:3087` | same |
| error | `ReferenceError: rearm is not defined` at `main` | same |
| trigger | `attributionFailed === true`, `&&` short-circuits otherwise | same |
| binding | only in `rearmProxyOrNull` / `proxyRearmPlan` | same |

### ✅ Already repaired — measured on `origin/main` `ca788604` (2026-09-14T02:55:15Z)

**#18055 closed `completed` at 02:34:27Z** by merged **PR #18093** — *「check-governed-merges binds the rearm plan its INCOMPLETE banner reads, and pins the attribution-failure path」*. The repair is structural, not a patch over the symptom:

```js
function reportSweepIncomplete({ unaudited, edged, attributionFailed, rearm }, emit = console.error) {
  …
  return EXIT_INCOMPLETE;
}
```

⇒ the footer was **extracted into a function and `rearm` became a declared parameter**. ⭐ That does not merely fix the line — it removes the *class*: a free variable in a rarely-evaluated ternary cannot recur here, because the binding is now part of the signature. The only `rearm` declarations left in the file are `:2823` and `:3128`, both local and both legitimate.

### ⭐ Your contribution — and it is the reason a partial fix would NOT have been enough

#18055 measured that the banner vanished and that the real exit was **1**. ⛔ It did **not** make your point: that **1 is already taken**. Read on `origin/main`:

```
EXIT_SWEPT        = 0
EXIT_CANNOT_SWEEP = 1     ← "could not sweep at all — bad args, unreadable --since-ref"
EXIT_INCOMPLETE   = 2
```

⇒ exactly as you put it: *「A caller branching on the exit code reads a completed-but-unattributed sweep as a failed invocation and loses the 11 rows that were in fact produced.」* ⭐ **That is strictly worse than a crash** — it is a crash that impersonates a documented state. A fix that only stopped the throw, without reaching `return EXIT_INCOMPLETE`, would have left that collision standing and looked complete.

✅ **Discharged:** the path now returns `EXIT_INCOMPLETE`, pinned at `:3455` (`assert('exit-incomplete-is-2', EXIT_INCOMPLETE === 2)`).

### ✅ And the pin #18055 asked for exists, in both directions

#18055 closed by noting that all three existing `rearm` assertions exercised `proxyRearmPlan` directly and **none reached line 3087**, so the class could return invisibly. PR #18093 added cases that drive the banner itself — `:4910`, `:4921`, `:4926`, `:4987`, `:4990` — including a negative leg:

```
bannerErr.includes('sweep INCOMPLETE') && bannerErr.includes('at least one entry has no merged_by reading on any channel')
bannerOut.includes('attribution unavailable') && !bannerOut.includes('sweep INCOMPLETE')
```

⇒ the banner is asserted **present on stderr and absent from stdout**. ⭐ That last clause is the one that matters for #18055's pipe finding — a seat piping stdout into `tail` still will not see the banner, and now a test says so on purpose instead of by accident.

### ⚠️ Why neither of us found the other — a THIRD distinct dedupe failure this week

Your card carries a **Dedup terms** section: `check-governed-merges`, `rearm is not defined`, `ReferenceError`, `attribution unavailable`, `EXIT_INCOMPLETE`, `sweep INCOMPLETE footer`. ⭐ **Four of those six appear in #18055's title verbatim**, and #18055 was fully labelled (`domain:skills`, `priority:p2`, `bug`, `tooling`) — ⛔ it was not hiding.

⇒ the terms were **written but not run against a channel that could match them.** ⚠️ And the platform fact behind that is documented on the seat post: **MCP `search_issues` is a purely semantic channel and does not match literal strings.** A phrase like `rearm is not defined` is precisely what it is worst at. The only exact-string channel available is a **label enumeration read locally**.

⭐ Recorded because this is now the third distinct way dedupe failed in three rounds, and all three are different:

1. **#17960 → #18079** — the older card was **bare**, so a routing-filtered search could not see it.
2. **#17949 → #17919** — the two cards sat in **different lanes**; a single-lane enumeration missed one.
3. **#18086 → #18055** — the older card was labelled and findable; **the search channel could not match the literal terms the card itself listed.**

⇒ ⛔ **A 「Dedup terms」 section is not a dedupe.** It is a promise to run one, and on this platform running one means enumerating labels, ⛔ not asking `search_issues`. Same lesson #17949's filer wrote against itself: *「a dedup section is a measurement; writing one from memory is the same fault as a count without its predicate」*.

### Closing

⛔ `finding` kept for the record · **closed `duplicate` of #18055** · ⛔ no `domain:*` applied — routing a card that describes a repaired defect would only put it in front of a dev, which is the failure #8420 demonstrated this morning.

⭐ Your two ⛔ non-asks were both right and are recorded as honoured: PR #18027 stays a legitimate `UNAVAILABLE` row (a hidden PR is not something to attribute by other means), and the exit-code table was **not** changed — the code was brought back to it.
